PullRequest.Title: Improve customization message UI and migration behavior
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request enhances the customization messages and migration functionality in the chat feature. Key changes include:

- **Distinguishing Customizations**: The migration message now specifies the number of workspace and user customizations separately, e.g., "Found 2 workspace and 2 user customizations..."
- **Summary Option**: Introduced a new `summary` mode for the migration hint, displayed once per session, providing a comprehensive overview of instructions, skills, and agents.
- **Improved Navigation**: Clicking on "Review customizations" now directs users to the migration page and focuses on the first actionable control.
- **Exclusion of Disabled Customizations**: Disabled customizations are no longer counted in availability totals.

The implementation ensures that existing behaviors remain intact while enhancing user experience and clarity in customization management. All relevant tests have been updated and passed successfully.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added invocation, its O(plugins + files) remote-filesystem implementation, and the await-before-dispatch call path are explicit. Only prevalence and exact duration are uncertain because the mode must be enabled and the expansion cache must be cold or invalidated.
Findings.PerformanceResource: agent-host filesystem RPCs and markdown-file reads
Findings.PerformanceScaling: On a cold provider cache, work grows with the number of installed plugins and their customization files: each plugin expands four canonical directories and reads metadata for every skill plus every agent/instruction markdown file. Expansions are launched concurrently; warm calls avoid plugin expansion until a plugin nonce/label changes, but still rebuild the full item collection.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: The first request in each Summary-mode chat cannot proceed to agent dispatch until the slowest new enumeration completes, increasing first-response latency and creating an IPC/I/O burst; cancellation does not stop it because the added call uses CancellationToken.None.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, customization hint collection awaited only the three migration computations. No hint mode invoked provideChatSessionCustomizations, so sending a chat request did not trigger full plugin-content expansion for summary counts.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Summary mode now calls provideChatSessionCustomizations from computeMigrationHint. ChatService awaits that hint together with hooks/instructions before building and dispatching the agent request.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 74 adds `harness.itemProvider?.provideChatSessionCustomizations(sessionResource, CancellationToken.None)` only for the new summary mode, placing the full enumeration on a path that previously performed no such provider call.
Findings.Title: Keep full customization enumeration off the first-send critical path
Findings.Impact: With Summary enabled and a cold cache—for example, the first chat after startup with several remote agent-host plugins—the user's first send waits for directory resolution/listing and per-file metadata reads across all plugins before the agent starts responding.
Findings.Evidence: The added line calls the harness item provider with CancellationToken.None. AgentCustomizationItemProvider.provideChatSessionCustomizations expands every plugin via Promise.all; AgentCustomizationContentExpander resolves agents/skills/commands/rules and reads each skill and agent/rule markdown file. vscode-agent-host filesystem operations map to remote resourceResolve/resourceList/resourceRead calls. In ChatService.sendRequest, collectCustomizationMigrationHint is awaited in Step 2 before Step 4 constructs the agent request and before provider invocation.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not await full item-provider enumeration before dispatching the chat request. Reuse/coalesce an invalidatable provider-item snapshot that is warmed outside the send path, or publish the summary notification after agent dispatch; also pass the request cancellation token so abandoned sends stop outstanding scans.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send the first chat request in the new Summary migration-hint mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatService awaits hooks, automatic instructions, and computeMigrationHint in one Promise.all before it builds and dispatches the agent request. The newly requested customization summary is therefore on the first-response critical path, not background work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover local/user agent, instruction, and prompt migration candidates
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three logical prompt-type lists per shown hint; underlying local/user discovery is generally cached/coalesced by PromptsService and invalidated by file/config/workspace events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Once/Always migration hints already ran these same three migration computations; Summary reuses that behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before agent dispatch as part of computeMigrationHint.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/list each plugin's agents, skills, commands, and rules directories and read customization markdown metadata over the agent-host filesystem
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold cache: up to four directory resolutions/listings per plugin plus one read per skill and per agent/instruction markdown file; warm cache: zero plugin expansion RPCs until nonce/label invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: computeMigrationHint did not call provideChatSessionCustomizations, so hint collection did not trigger this full plugin enumeration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The slowest plugin/file operation delays construction and dispatch of the first agent request; all plugins/files can burst concurrently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve MCP support scope for the current working directories
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One acquired support scope per computed hint, grouped across all servers in the session scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing migration hints already acquired and awaited the same MCP support scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the hint Promise before dispatch, but it already existed for Once/Always hints and is not increased by the summary enumeration line.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Collect and parse automatic instructions for request context
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One collection per chat turn over applicable instruction files, with parsing/reads driven by the request context.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Automatic instruction collection already ran on this request path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already awaited before dispatch in parallel with the hint; the PR does not add this boundary, but the new plugin scan competes with it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cold cardinality is the number of agent-host plugins plus their skill, agent, and instruction files. Each plugin is expanded once per nonce/label while the provider lives; every new Summary session still reconstructs/counts all returned items, but warm expansion-cache calls avoid the remote plugin scans.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The hint's migration checks and full item enumeration run concurrently with hooks/instruction collection. AgentCustomizationItemProvider starts expansion for all plugins in one Promise.all; each expansion resolves four canonical directories and concurrently reads eligible metadata files, with no limiter or backpressure.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt-file migration lists use PromptsService cached promises after their locator events are initialized and invalidate on watched changes. Agent plugin expansions cache children by plugin URI, nonce, and label, so the remote fan-out is cold-start/invalidation work rather than per-session successful fan-out. The new outer provider call is not shared with chat request collection, and CancellationToken.None leaves cold work running after request cancellation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff-added provider call, full expansion implementation, remote filesystem mapping, concurrent fan-out, and await-before-dispatch path are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Summary must be enabled (directly or by experiment), and exact delay depends on plugin count, remote latency, file count, and whether expansions were previously warmed. The critical-path placement and cold O(plugins + files) RPC fan-out are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: the new summary count eagerly enumerates all provider items over remote filesystem boundaries before first request dispatch. It should use an invalidatable shared snapshot/background notification and request cancellation rather than blocking send.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send chat requests with existing Once or Always migration hints
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The same three migration computations remain awaited before request dispatch whenever a hint is eligible. Once is skipped after session state records the first displayed hint; Always repeats per request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three prompt-type lists per eligible hint, with existing PromptsService caching/invalidation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical migration computations and boundary cardinality were already used for hints.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Same await-before-dispatch behavior as the base revision.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Await MCP support discovery for the session scope
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped scope per eligible hint.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Migration candidates across local/user prompt stores and the MCP server group for the active session. Candidate counting now performs a few linear in-memory filters over the already-returned candidates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: User-data, prompt-file, and MCP migration computations remain in a three-way Promise.all. No new concurrency or boundary is introduced when includeCustomizationSummary is false.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt-file lists retain their existing watched caches; source-folder lookup and MCP support use existing ownership. The new temporary concatenated candidate array is request-scoped and bounded by customization count.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that no material performance mechanism changed for non-summary modes.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Candidate counts vary by workspace, but the newly added in-memory storage filters are small relative to unchanged discovery work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the behavior change is formatting/count classification over existing results, without additional expensive boundaries or meaningful retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Click Review customizations from a migration hint and open the migration page
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command opens/focuses the management editor, then the new migration branch awaits showCustomizationMigrationPage; that method refreshes migration information before selecting and rendering the first enabled category.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List agent, instruction, and prompt files to compute migration candidates
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to three prompt-type list requests per refresh; overlapping calls generally share PromptsService cached promises after cache initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening the editor initialized migration data asynchronously but did not await another refresh specifically to deep-link into migration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The explicit refresh is awaited before the migration page is shown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compute writable destination source folders from active agent-host customization state
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per distinct target type for each overlapping refresh; based on in-memory session customization arrays for the agent-host provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing editor migration refreshes already performed these lookups.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by each computeMigration, but does not cross a remote boundary for the active agent-host implementation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Enabled migration categories and their candidate prompt files. One explicit refresh is added per migration deep-link click; editor creation/session autoruns may already have an in-flight refresh.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Editor-created/session-triggered refreshes and the explicit refresh can overlap. A sequence number suppresses stale commits but does not cancel prior work; cached prompt-list promises can coalesce the main filesystem discovery, while source-folder computations may repeat.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: PromptsService caches prompt-list promises with watcher invalidation. Migration results themselves are not cached in the editor, but agent-host provideSourceFolders is derived from already-materialized customization state. Reopening an existing editor still performs one explicit freshness refresh.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that an extra refresh is invoked; low that it causes additional expensive boundary work after cache/coalescing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether the explicit refresh duplicates a cold filesystem scan depends on cache initialization and timing. The common agent-host destination lookup is in-memory, so a concrete user-visible regression from the extra refresh is not established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the refresh is bounded to a deliberate user click and is needed for fresh category selection; available evidence does not prove a material extra I/O or latency regression beyond cached/coalesced work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 13 changed files. Reported one diff-introduced first-send IPC/filesystem fan-out in Summary mode. Regular hint formatting and migration deep-link refresh behavior did not meet the evidence threshold for additional performance findings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
